title: Adaptive cardinality reduction for inference KPIs
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Inference traffic generates extremely high-cardinality labels (prompt_id, user_prompt_hash, dataset_tag, model_revision_tag) that overwhelm Prometheus scraping and downstream SLI computation. This causes slow queries, unbounded series growth, alert noise, and heavy storage costs. We need a pipeline-level approach that preserves useful SLI signals (latency percentiles, error rates, model-level aggregation) while preventing unbounded cardinality from client-supplied or ephemeral labels.

Proposal: Implement an "adaptive cardinality reduction" component inside the telemetry gateway that applies a small set of deterministic transformations to incoming OTLP metrics and Prometheus remote-write streams: 1) label allowlist/denylist at ingestion with configurable regex; 2) probabilistic k-anonymity grouping for free-text labels using bucketing by hash prefix; 3) sampled per-tenant detailed metrics (sticky sampling) for debugging; 4) an optional privacy mode that drops or truncates user-level identifiers; 5) histogram bucketing normalization for latency to ensure stable cardinality across model types. The component will expose configuration via Console and will emit audit metrics documenting reductions applied.

Why unique: Rather than a static scrubber or global label blacklist, this design adapts to each tenant's traffic shape, preserves per-model and per-route SLIs, and keeps a small deterministic sample for incident triage. It aligns with Redwood's multi-tenant goals and Dedicated/Private constraints (configurable per-deployment).
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry gateway has a feature flag toggling adaptive cardinality reduction
Config UI allows per-tenant allowlist/denylist and sampling rate override
Inbound OTLP metrics with high-cardinality labels are reduced to bounded cardinality without breaking model-level SLIs
End-to-end tests demonstrate 95% reduction in unique series for synthetic high-cardinality load while latency and error SLIs remain within 1% of baseline
Audit metrics show counts of labels dropped, hashed, or sampled and are visible in Console
tasks: Design: define canonical rules for label transformations and k-anonymity bucketing (owner: Liam)
Gateway: implement allowlist/denylist filter and label hashing module (owner: Infra team)
Gateway: implement sticky sampling for detailed traces and sampled metrics (owner: Telemetry team)
Console: add UI to configure per-tenant policies and view audit metrics (owner: Console UX)
Testing: create synthetic high-cardinality generator and integration tests (owner: SRE)
Docs: write runbook and configuration examples for Dedicated/Private deployments (owner: Docs)
Rollout: staged rollout with feature flag and canary per region (owner: Observability release lead)
risk_and_mitigation: Risks: accidental dropping of important identifiers leading to loss of debugability; increased CPU cost in gateway due to hashing/bucketing; tenant confusion if SLIs change. Mitigations: conservative defaults (denylist only off by default), sticky sampled streams for debugging, audit metrics and automated regression tests, limit CPU work via async processing and circuit breaker when load spikes.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind telemetry-gateway feature flag in staging. 2) Enable for internal tenant + synthetic load tests and validate metric series counts and SLI stability. 3) Canary for 5% of hosted tenants with observability and database backfill disabled. 4) Expand to Dedicated after manual review and per-customer opt-in. 5) Offer 'privacy-mode' for Private installs with explicit config. Rollback path: disable feature flag and replay raw ingestion for last 24h where needed.
